verdicts.title: Karchmer-Wigderson Games for Hazard-free Computation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We present a Karchmer-Wigderson game to study the complexity of hazard-free formulas. This new game is both a generalization of the monotone Karchmer-Wigderson game and an analog of the classical Boolean Karchmer-Wigderson game. Therefore, it acts as a bridge between the existing monotone and general games.
  Using this game, we prove hazard-free formula size and depth lower bounds that are provably stronger than those possible by the standard technique of transferring results from monotone comp
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a Karchmer-Wigderson game variant for hazard-free formulas with size/depth lower bounds, but says nothing about oracle-augmented depth, coarse geometry, Roe algebras, or relativization barriers — it only shares the general KW-game vocabulary.

verdicts.title: Roe algebras of coarse spaces via coarse geometric modules
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We provide a construction of Roe (C*-)algebras of general coarse spaces in terms of coarse geometric modules. This extends the classical theory of Roe algebras of metric spaces and gives a unified framework to deal with either uniform or non-uniform Roe algebras, algebras of operators of controlled propagation, and algebras of quasi-local operators; both in the metric and general coarse geometric setting. The key new definitions are that of coarse geometric module and coarse support of operators
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a general construction of Roe algebras via coarse geometric modules and studies structural/K-theoretic properties; it makes no claim about oracle-augmented boolean functions, KW-depth, or relativization barriers, so it neither supports nor refutes the specific oracle-collapse claim about κ(f^A).

verdicts.title: Multiparty Karchmer-Wigderson Games and Threshold Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We suggest a generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson communication games to the multiparty setting. Our generalization turns out to be tightly connected to circuits consisting of threshold gates. This allows us to obtain new explicit constructions of such circuits for several functions. In particular, we provide an explicit (polynomial-time computable) log-depth monotone formula for Majority function, consisting only of 3-bit majority gates and variables. This resolves a conjecture of Cohen et al.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a multiparty generalization of KW games connected to threshold circuits and Majority formulas, with no mention of oracle relativization, coarse geometry, Roe algebras, or the κ invariant addressed by the conjecture.
